Name: BC Backcountry Lodges (Selkirks & Kootenays)
Includes: Valhalla Range; Battle Range (Selkirks); Kokanee & Kaslo area
Pitch: Fly in by helicopter to a timber lodge at treeline, then tour from the door for a week of Interior BC powder.

Name: Baffin Island (Clyde River & Sam Ford Fjord)
Pitch: Big-wall fjords and 1,000 m couloirs straight off the sea ice, from tent camps reached by Inuit-run snowmobile.

Name: Banff (Lake Louise, Sunshine, Norquay)
Includes: Lake Louise; Sunshine Village; Mt Norquay
Pitch: Three resorts inside a national park; spectacular scenery, cold, long season.

Name: Big White
Pitch: Family ski-in/ski-out village with dry 'champagne powder'; famous for fog (snow ghosts).

Name: Chic-Chocs (Gaspésie)
Getting there: Montréal, then a long drive / Mont-Joli
Pitch: Eastern Canada's best snow: open alpine bowls above the St. Lawrence, with huts and lodges.

Name: Fernie
Pitch: Five big alpine bowls and lots of snow in a historic town.

Name: Gros Morne & Humber Valley
Pitch: Fjords, tablelands and treeless bowls in a UNESCO park, with Marble Mountain's lifts for stormy days.

Name: Interior BC Heli & Cat (Selkirks, Monashees, Bugaboos)
Getting there: Calgary / Kelowna, plus heli or road transfer
Includes: CMH Bugaboos; Mike Wiegele (Blue River); Baldface (cat)
Pitch: The birthplace of heli-skiing: endless old-growth tree runs and glaciers from remote lodges (CMH, Mike Wiegele, Baldface cat).

Name: Kicking Horse
Pitch: Steep chutes and big bowls above Golden; on the Powder Highway with Revelstoke.

Name: Kootenays (Red Mountain & Whitewater)
Pitch: Old-school, steep tree skiing in Rossland and Nelson; lots of cat skiing nearby.

Name: Mont-Tremblant
Pitch: Eastern North America's flagship resort village with French-Canadian charm.

Name: Revelstoke
Pitch: Biggest lift-served vertical in North America (1,713 m); hub for cat and heli skiing and Rogers Pass.

Name: Rogers Pass
Getting there: Calgary 4h / Kelowna 3h; base in Revelstoke or Golden
Pitch: Iconic Selkirk backcountry on the Trans-Canada Highway: huge snowfall, glaciers, trees, and huts.

Name: Wapta Icefield Traverse
Pitch: The Rockies' classic hut-to-hut glacier traverse (Bow, Peyto, Balfour, Scott Duncan huts) off the Icefields Parkway.

Name: Whistler Blackcomb
Pitch: North America's biggest ski area: two mountains, 3,300+ ha, glaciers on top, rain risk at the base.

Name: East Greenland (Tasiilaq)
Pitch: The Ammassalik Alps: jagged peaks and sea ice; very remote.

Name: Greenland Ice Cap Crossing
Pitch: The classic polar journey: about 550 km and four weeks pulling a sled across the ice cap, coast to coast.

Name: West Greenland (Maniitsoq & Sisimiut)
Getting there: Kangerlussuaq / Nuuk, then boat or heli
Pitch: Expedition-yacht and heli skiing in empty fjords. Maniitsoq is called the 'Venice of the Arctic'.

Name: Alyeska
Pitch: Sea-level base and steep upper bowls; pairs with Turnagain Pass touring and Chugach heli.

Name: Aspen Snowmass
Includes: Aspen Mountain (Ajax); Snowmass; Aspen Highlands; Buttermilk
Pitch: Four mountains (Snowmass, Ajax, Highlands, Buttermilk) and a glamorous town; Highland Bowl hike for experts.

Name: Big Sky
Pitch: Huge, uncrowded terrain under Lone Peak's steep tram line.

Name: Cascade Volcanoes (Hood, Rainier, Baker, Adams)
Pitch: Spring corn-snow road trip, skiing big glaciated volcanoes from the summit.

Name: Chugach / Valdez Heli
Pitch: The steep spines of ski films. Coastal Alaska snow sticks to 50° faces. Very weather-dependent.

Name: Colorado Hut Systems (10th Mountain)
Pitch: Network of 30+ backcountry huts between Vail, Aspen and Leadville.

Name: Cottonwood Canyons (Alta, Snowbird, Brighton, Solitude)
Pitch: 'Greatest Snow on Earth': light, frequent lake-effect snow and steep terrain, 40 minutes from a major airport.

Name: Crested Butte
Pitch: Funky old mining town; the Extreme Limits are among the steepest lift-served terrain in the US.

Name: Denali & Ruth Gorge
Pitch: North America's highest peak, guided on skis since 2022, or glacier ski touring under the granite walls of Ruth Gorge.

Name: Eastern Sierra Backcountry
Pitch: Huge couloirs above Highway 395 (Bishop, June Lake, Mammoth); world-class spring corn.

Name: Haines Heli
Pitch: Alaska's other heli mecca: big glaciated lines, smaller and quieter than Valdez.

Name: Jackson Hole
Includes: Jackson Hole Mountain Resort; Grand Targhee
Pitch: Steep, big-vertical resort with Corbet's Couloir and world-class sidecountry; Grand Targhee next door for deep snow.

Name: Lake Tahoe
Includes: Palisades Tahoe (+ Alpine Meadows); Northstar; Sugar Bowl; Heavenly; Kirkwood; Mt Rose; Donner Summit; Carson Pass; Mt Rose backcountry; Desolation Wilderness
Pitch: A cluster of big resorts around the lake: huge snowfall years, sunny between storms, and very variable from season to season.

Name: Mammoth Mountain
Pitch: High-altitude volcano with one of the longest seasons in the US, often into June.

Name: Mount Shasta
Pitch: A lone 4,322 m volcano with 2,000 m spring corn runs on every side, plus Lassen's volcano park 90 minutes away.

Name: Mt Washington (Tuckerman Ravine)
Pitch: Classic Eastern spring pilgrimage to the ravine headwall.

Name: Mt. Baker
Pitch: Record-holding snowfall, rustic lifts, and sidecountry and backcountry access off the top. Core skier culture.

Name: Northern Vermont (Stowe, Jay Peak, Sugarbush)
Pitch: Best snow in the US Northeast; classic New England tree skiing.

Name: Ogden Valley (Snowbasin & Powder Mountain)
Pitch: Uncrowded Utah: Snowbasin's Olympic terrain and lodges, and Powder Mountain's cap on daily ticket sales.

Name: Park City & Deer Valley
Pitch: The US's largest single resort plus Deer Valley's luxury groomers; a real town with food and nightlife. Family-friendly.

Name: San Juans Backcountry (Red Mountain Pass)
Pitch: High-alpine road-access touring between Silverton and Ouray, with yurts and huts.

Name: Sierra High Route
Pitch: The 'Sierra High Route': a committing 6-7 day spring traverse across the High Sierra near Mt Whitney, camping or tenting rather than huts.

Name: Silverton Mountain
Pitch: One chairlift, all expert, avalanche-gear-required, mostly guided. Optional heli drops.

Name: Steamboat
Pitch: 'Champagne powder' and famous tree skiing; ranch-town feel.

Name: Summit County (Breckenridge, Keystone, A-Basin, Copper)
Includes: Breckenridge; Keystone; Arapahoe Basin; Copper Mountain
Pitch: High-altitude cluster with lots of choice; A-Basin skis into June.

Name: Sun Valley
Pitch: America's first destination resort: long consistent fall-line groomers on Bald Mountain.

Name: Taos Ski Valley
Pitch: Steep, high, sunny; hike-to Kachina and Highline ridges. Adobe culture.

Name: Telluride
Pitch: Stunning box canyon town with a mix of family groomers and hike-to expert terrain.

Name: Teton Pass & Grand Teton backcountry
Pitch: Road-accessed touring off Teton Pass; spring ski mountaineering in Grand Teton NP.

Name: Vail & Beaver Creek
Pitch: Massive groomed front side plus the Back Bowls; polished, expensive resort villages.

Name: Washington Pass (North Cascades)
Pitch: Each spring the North Cascades Highway reopens onto a week's worth of granite couloirs and glacier lines.

Name: Winter Park & Mary Jane
Pitch: Denver's local giant: Mary Jane's famous bumps, Winter Park's cruisers, and a direct ski train from Union Station.

Name: Wolf Creek
Pitch: The most snow in Colorado, an independent family-owned hill, and a cheap ticket. Pairs with Taos or Silverton.

Name: Bariloche (Cerro Catedral)
Pitch: South America's largest resort over a Patagonian lake city; great sidecountry and Frey touring nearby.

Name: Bariloche Backcountry (Refugio Frey)
Pitch: Granite spires and couloirs around Refugio Frey, accessed from Catedral.

Name: Las Leñas
Pitch: The Marte chair accesses vast steep chute terrain. Famous among freeriders, when Marte runs.

Name: Ushuaia (Cerro Castor)
Pitch: The southernmost resort on Earth; low-elevation but dependable cold snow; backcountry touring around.

Name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
Pitch: Ski onto the largest ice field outside the poles, under the east faces of Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre.

Name: Araucanía Volcanoes (Pucón)
Pitch: Road trip skiing perfect volcanic cones (Villarrica, Llaima, Lonquimay) with hot springs and araucaria forests.

Name: Nevados de Chillán
Pitch: Volcano resort with hot springs and Chile's longest run; big sidecountry.

Name: Portillo
Pitch: Legendary single-hotel resort on Laguna del Inca; steep chutes like the Super C.

Name: Santiago Three Valleys (Valle Nevado, La Parva, El Colorado)
Includes: Valle Nevado; La Parva; El Colorado; Cajón del Maipo
Pitch: Big interconnected high-Andes terrain an hour from a capital city; heli-skiing on offer.

Name: Antarctic Peninsula (sail & ski)
Pitch: Ski from sea to summit from expedition yachts among icebergs and penguins. The trip of a lifetime.

Name: Grandvalira
Pitch: The Pyrenees' largest area, good value, and duty-free shopping.

Name: Arlberg (St. Anton, Lech, Zürs)
Pitch: Birthplace of Alpine skiing: steep ungroomed 'ski routes', big off-piste, and legendary après.

Name: Ischgl & Paznaun
Pitch: Cross-border to Samnaun (Switzerland); high, snow-sure, party town.

Name: Kitzbühel & SkiWelt
Pitch: Historic town, the Streif, and a huge linked area; low altitude, so check snow conditions.

Name: Saalbach Hinterglemm
Pitch: Big, cruisy ski circus with lively après.

Name: Stubai Alps huts
Pitch: Austria's classic hut-touring week: dense hut network (Franz-Senn, Amberger), lots of 3,000 m summits, 40 minutes from Innsbruck.

Name: Zillertal (Mayrhofen, Hintertux)
Pitch: A valley of linked areas, with year-round glacier skiing at Hintertux.

Name: Ötztal (Sölden, Obergurgl)
Pitch: Two glaciers and Austria's most reliable snow; Obergurgl is quiet and family-oriented.

Name: Ötztal Alps huts (Vent)
Pitch: High glaciated hut tours to the Wildspitze, Austria's second-highest peak.

Name: Silvretta & Rätikon huts
Pitch: Friendly glaciated hut touring with lots of 3,000 m peaks; good first hut trip.

Name: Pirin & Bansko
Pitch: Alpine limestone peaks up to 2,914 m Vihren above a cheap, lively resort town: tour by day, lifts as backup.

Name: Altay: Jikepulin-Hemu
Pitch: Bone-dry powder in the hills that claim to be the birthplace of skiing, beside a Tuvan log-cabin village.
Travel advisory: Xinjiang has pervasive police checkpoints and surveillance; border areas (including Hemu/Kanas and the Pamir) need extra permits, and some travellers also weigh the region's human-rights situation. Check your government's travel advice.

Name: Muztagh Ata
Pitch: The 7,546 m 'father of ice mountains': the classic first 7,000 m peak to ski, with a broad glacier from near the summit.
Travel advisory: Xinjiang has pervasive police checkpoints and surveillance; border areas (including Hemu/Kanas and the Pamir) need extra permits, and some travellers also weigh the region's human-rights situation. Check your government's travel advice.

Name: Ecuador's Volcanoes (Cayambe, Cotopaxi, Chimborazo)
Pitch: Ski glaciated volcanoes on the equator, ending on Chimborazo: the point on Earth farthest from its centre.

Name: Alpe d'Huez
Pitch: Sunny south-facing giant with the 16 km Sarenne black run.

Name: Chamonix Mont-Blanc
Includes: Grands Montets; Aiguille du Midi (Vallée Blanche); Brévent-Flégère; Le Tour-Balme
Pitch: The world capital of alpinism and freeride: Vallée Blanche, Grands Montets, huge glaciated terrain. Gateway to the Haute Route.

Name: Corsica: Alta Strada
Pitch: The GR20 on skis: a week-long haute route along the granite spine of a Mediterranean island, with sea views.

Name: La Grave – La Meije
Pitch: Just a cable car and 2,000 m of ungroomed, glaciated high-mountain freeride. Mythic. Pairs with Serre Chevalier.

Name: Les 3 Vallées (Courchevel, Méribel, Val Thorens)
Includes: Courchevel; Méribel; Val Thorens; Les Menuires
Pitch: The world's largest linked ski area (600 km of pistes); ski-in/ski-out at altitude.

Name: Paradiski (Les Arcs, La Plagne)
Pitch: Huge linked area with purpose-built villages; very family-friendly; train-accessible.

Name: Val d'Isère & Tignes
Pitch: High, snow-sure, and legendary off-piste (Espace Killy); glacier skiing at Tignes.

Name: Vanoise Haute Route
Pitch: Hut-to-hut glacier traverse through France's first national park, between Pralognan and Val d'Isère.

Name: Écrins huts
Pitch: Big, wild glaciated massif around the Barre des Écrins, with the Dôme des Écrins as a classic 4,000 m ski summit. Wilder and quieter than Chamonix.

Name: Haute Route (Chamonix → Zermatt)
Pitch: The classic 6-7 day hut-to-hut glacier traverse. Bucket list.

Name: Portes du Soleil (Avoriaz, Morzine, Champéry)
Pitch: Cross-border circuit of 12 resorts; lower altitude, so check snow conditions.

Name: Courmayeur & Skyway
Pitch: Italian side of Mont Blanc: Skyway Monte Bianco gives big glacier freeride; great food; 20 min from Chamonix.

Name: Dolomiti Superski (Val Gardena, Alta Badia, Cortina)
Includes: Val Gardena; Alta Badia; Cortina d'Ampezzo; Arabba & Marmolada; Kronplatz
Pitch: 1,200 km of pistes in UNESCO limestone towers, with incredible food and huts. Sunny cruising; snowmaking-reliant.

Name: Fanes-Senes-Braies (Dolomites)
Pitch: Quiet Dolomites touring through a nature park of limestone plateaus, with excellent rifugi (Fanes, Lavarella) between Cortina and Alta Badia.

Name: Gran Paradiso
Pitch: A 'ski-able' 4,000er from the Vittorio Emanuele hut, in a national park full of ibex.

Name: Livigno
Pitch: High, cold, duty-free valley, snow-sure with great parks.

Name: Monte Rosa (Alagna, Gressoney)
Pitch: Alagna is a freeride mecca: few pistes, huge lift-served off-piste, legal heli drops.

Name: Ortler & Cevedale
Pitch: High glaciated touring from the Casati and Branca huts: Cevedale and Palon de la Mare are classic ski summits.

Name: Valle Maira
Pitch: An Occitan valley with no lifts and hundreds of mapped tours, stone hamlets and some of the best food in the Alps.

Name: Altai Tavan Bogd
Pitch: Yurt-based ski touring on Mongolia's highest glaciers, hosted by Kazakh eagle-hunting families.

Name: Annapurna Sanctuary
Pitch: Ski touring inside a ring of 7,000 and 8,000 m peaks from the lodges at Annapurna Base Camp.

Name: Mera Peak
Pitch: The Himalaya's classic ski objective: a gentle glacier from 6,476 m with Everest, Lhotse and Makalu on the horizon.

Name: Popova Šapka Cat Skiing
Pitch: Europe's oldest cat-skiing operation, in the wild Šar Mountains above a small Balkan resort.

Name: Hunza & Naltar
Pitch: Ski touring under 7,000 m Karakoram giants, with Hunza's apricot-orchard villages and legendary hospitality.
Travel advisory: Several governments advise against travel to parts of Pakistan; Gilgit-Baltistan is generally treated differently from border regions. Check your government's current advice and use a registered local operator.

Name: High Tatras
Pitch: Compact granite range with steep couloirs and mountain huts (chaty), cheap and accessible from Kraków or Poprad.

Name: Julian Alps (Kanin & Triglav)
Pitch: Limestone karst peaks above emerald rivers: day tours from Kanin's lifts and a hut traverse around Triglav.

Name: Baqueira-Beret
Pitch: Spain's best resort, on the Atlantic-facing Pyrenees with good off-piste.

Name: Pyrenees Haute Route
Pitch: Hut-to-hut across the central Pyrenees (Gavarnie to Aneto) with Spanish food and fewer people than the Alps.

Name: Andermatt
Pitch: Gemsstock's steep freeride terrain at a snow crossroads catching storms from north and south.

Name: Bernese Oberland Haute Route
Getting there: Zurich / Bern by train to Jungfraujoch
Pitch: Ride the train to the Jungfraujoch and tour the Aletsch glacier world between big huts (Konkordia, Finsteraarhorn): Switzerland's grandest hut tour.

Name: Davos Klosters
Pitch: Five ski areas, long off-piste descents to villages, home of the SLF avalanche institute.

Name: Engelberg
Pitch: Titlis' 2,000 m freeride descents (Laub, Galtiberg); a Scandinavian freeride community; easy from Zurich.

Name: Jungfrau Region (Wengen, Grindelwald, Mürren)
Pitch: Car-free villages under the Eiger; the scenery is the point.

Name: Laax Flims
Pitch: Europe's freestyle capital: huge terrain parks, and a glacier.

Name: Saas-Fee
Pitch: Glacier village surrounded by thirteen 4,000 m peaks; snow-sure and quieter than Zermatt.

Name: St. Moritz & Engadin
Pitch: Sunny high valley with Corviglia, Diavolezza glacier runs, and glamour.

Name: Verbier (4 Vallées)
Pitch: Freeride capital (Xtreme Verbier); off-piste right off the lifts, plus a huge linked piste network.

Name: Zermatt (+ Cervinia)
Pitch: Car-free village under the Matterhorn, glacier skiing, and lunch in Italy. End of the Haute Route.

Name: Erciyes & Cappadocia
Pitch: Ski an extinct 3,917 m volcano by day and sleep in a Cappadocian cave hotel among the balloons.

Name: Mount Ararat
Pitch: Ski the 5,137 m volcano where Noah's Ark is said to rest, with mule support to camp and views into Iran and Armenia.
Travel advisory: Ararat is a military border zone: a climbing permit through a licensed Turkish agency is required and takes weeks. Check your government's advice for eastern Türkiye.

Name: Scottish Highlands (Cairngorms & Glencoe)
Includes: CairnGorm Mountain; Glencoe Mountain; Nevis Range
Pitch: Wild, wind-scoured Highland plateaus and gullies, with whisky and bothies after; brilliant when it's on.

Name: Amirsoy & Chimgan
Pitch: New lifts and old Soviet runs in the Tian Shan, 90 minutes from Tashkent and a train ride from Samarkand.

Name: Troll Peninsula
Pitch: Peak-to-ocean heli and touring with long spring daylight and hot pools.

Name: Vatnajökull Crossing
Pitch: Europe's largest ice cap on skis: a week-plus pulling sleds over volcanoes buried under the ice.

Name: Westfjords
Pitch: Remote, sailboat-based fjord touring.

Name: Hemsedal
Pitch: Norway's leading resort, the 'Scandinavian Alps'; family plus decent steeps.

Name: Jotunheimen huts
Getting there: Oslo, then 5h drive or train to Otta
Pitch: Norway's highest mountains (Galdhøpiggen, Glittertind) on a DNT hut network: classic Easter and spring touring, glacier day trips from Juvasshytta and Spiterstulen.

Name: Lofoten
Pitch: Dramatic peaks out of the sea; boat-based touring and fishing villages.

Name: Lyngen Alps
Pitch: The original sea-to-summit arctic touring: 1,500 m runs to the fjord, by lodge, ferry, or sailboat.

Name: Narvikfjellet
Pitch: Lift-accessed, steep fjord freeride above town; combine with Riksgränsen.

Name: Romsdal (Åndalsnes)
Pitch: Big-wall valley with steep couloirs and fjord descents.

Name: Senja
Pitch: Norway's second-largest island: quieter alternative to Lyngen.

Name: Sunnmøre Alps
Pitch: Fjord-to-summit classic (Hjørundfjord, Slogen) with historic hotels and boat access.

Name: Svalbard
Pitch: High-arctic ski expeditions by boat or snowmobile: glaciers, polar bears (armed guides required).

Name: Kebnekaise & Abisko
Pitch: Sweden's highest peak and arctic hut tours along the Kungsleden.

Name: Riksgränsen
Pitch: Arctic freeride: skiing under the midnight sun in May-June, plus heli. A train station on the slope.

Name: Sarek
Pitch: Sweden's wildest park: no huts, no roads, no trails, a week of tent and sled touring among glaciated peaks.

Name: Åre
Getting there: Åre Östersund (OSD), 1.5h; night train from Stockholm
Pitch: Scandinavia's biggest resort; lively village, off-piste on the top.

Name: Crete: Lefka Ori
Pitch: The White Mountains: ski-tour a lunar karst plateau with the Libyan Sea below, then eat in a taverna by the beach. Psiloritis is the other option.

Name: Mount Etna
Pitch: Ski-tour an active volcano above the Mediterranean, through steaming vents and black ash; two small lift areas too.

Name: Afriski
Pitch: One of only two ski resorts in Southern Africa, at 3,000 m in the 'Kingdom in the Sky'. Small and snowmaking-based, but unique.

Name: Oukaïmeden
Pitch: Ski Africa's highest lift-served slopes, an hour and a half from the Marrakech souks. Basic lifts, donkey 'lifts' and a big novelty factor.

Name: Toubkal & High Atlas
Pitch: Ski-tour North Africa's highest peak (4,167 m) from Berber villages and the Toubkal refuge, with mules carrying the gear.

Name: Sierra Nevada (Granada)
Pitch: Europe's southernmost major resort: ski in the morning, Alhambra in the afternoon, and on clear days you can see Africa.

Name: Gudauri
Pitch: Open, treeless freeride and cheap heli on the Georgian Military Highway; amazing food and wine.

Name: Svaneti (Mestia & Tetnuldi)
Pitch: Medieval tower villages under 4,000-5,000 m Caucasus peaks; touring off small lifts.

Name: Dizin & Shemshak
Pitch: High, dry Alborz powder an hour or two from Tehran: steep Shemshak, big open Dizin.
Travel advisory: Many governments advise against travel to Iran, and dual nationals face particular risks. Check your government's current advice before planning.

Name: Mount Damavand
Pitch: Ski a 5,610 m volcano, the highest in Asia, from the Bargah-e Sevom hut: a big-altitude spring descent.
Travel advisory: Many governments advise against travel to Iran, and dual nationals face particular risks. Check your government's current advice before planning.

Name: Mzaar & The Cedars
Pitch: Ski in the morning, Mediterranean beach in the afternoon. The Cedars sits above an ancient cedar grove.
Travel advisory: Advice for Lebanon changes quickly, and some areas are no-go. Check your government's current advice before planning.

Name: Kaçkar Mountains Heli
Pitch: Black Sea moisture onto the Pontic Alps: deep snow, lodge heli skiing.

Name: Dombai & Arkhyz
Pitch: Dramatic Caucasus peaks (Dombai) and a fast-growing modern resort (Arkhyz, voted Russia's best). Cheap, with big off-piste.
Travel advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

Name: Elbrus Region (Cheget & Elbrus)
Pitch: Old-school Soviet lifts on Cheget and the Elbrus cable car give huge, cheap freeride under Europe's highest peak.
Travel advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

Name: Kamchatka Heli
Pitch: Heli-skiing volcanoes that run down to the Pacific: one of the wildest heli destinations on Earth.
Travel advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

Name: Khibiny (Kirovsk)
Pitch: Arctic freeride and touring above the Kola Peninsula: open bowls, a long spring season, and midnight sun in May.
Travel advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

Name: Mount Elbrus Summit Descent
Pitch: Ski off the highest summit in Europe (5,642 m): a spring acclimatisation expedition with one of the world's great volcano descents.
Travel advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

Name: Sheregesh
Pitch: Siberia's powder capital: deep, very cold, dry snow in birch and fir forests, with a famous spring party scene.
Travel advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

Name: Sochi: Krasnaya Polyana
Includes: Rosa Khutor; Gazprom Laura & Polyana; Krasnaya Polyana resort
Pitch: The 2014 Olympic cluster: big modern lift systems 1 hour from the Black Sea, with lots of tree and sidecountry terrain.
Travel advisory: Many governments advise against all travel to Russia. Flights, visas, insurance and foreign card payments are heavily restricted, and rescue or consular help may be limited.

Name: Gulmarg
Pitch: Himalayan gondola to almost 4,000 m with vast freeride for little money.
Travel advisory: Some governments advise against travel to parts of Jammu & Kashmir. Check your government's current advice and your insurance.

Name: Manali Heli (Himachal)
Pitch: Long-running heli skiing in the Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar ranges, with 1,000 m-plus runs from Himalayan ridges.

Name: Asahidake
Pitch: A single ropeway up Hokkaido's highest (steaming) volcano: ungroomed, ultra-dry powder in birch forest.

Name: Furano & Central Hokkaido (Tomamu, Kamui)
Includes: Furano; Hoshino Tomamu; Kamui Ski Links
Pitch: Colder, drier inland Hokkaido powder; mix of resorts and a road trip to Asahidake.

Name: Hakkoda & Tohoku
Pitch: A ropeway into backcountry known for 'snow monsters' (rime-coated trees); deep, cold and few foreigners. Pair with Zao.

Name: Hakuba Valley
Includes: Happo-one; Hakuba 47 / Goryu; Hakuba Cortina; Iwatake
Pitch: Ten resorts under the Northern Alps, Olympic heritage, and serious backcountry in the Hakuba mountains.

Name: Kiroro & Sapporo resorts
Pitch: Kiroro is one of Hokkaido's deepest snow spots; Teine/Kokusai are day trips from Sapporo city.

Name: Mount Fuji (spring)
Pitch: Ski Japan's sacred volcano from the crater rim in late spring: a 1,500 m run with the whole country at your feet.

Name: Myoko, Nozawa & Shiga Kogen
Includes: Myoko Kogen; Lotte Arai; Nozawa Onsen; Shiga Kogen
Pitch: Onsen villages (Nozawa), Japan's largest linked area (Shiga), and Myoko/Lotte Arai's deep snow.

Name: Niseko & Rusutsu
Includes: Niseko United (Grand Hirafu, Annupuri, Village, Hanazono); Rusutsu; Mt Yōtei
Pitch: JAPOW ground zero: relentless light snow off the Sea of Japan, gate-controlled off-piste, onsens.

Name: Tateyama Kurobe
Pitch: Spring-only: the Alpine Route opens in mid-April to giant snow walls, giving access to huge Northern Alps couloirs from mountain huts at Murodo.

Name: Tokachi & Daisetsuzan Backcountry
Pitch: Hut-based and road-access touring (Fukiage, Sandan-yama) in famously dry snow.

Name: Almaty: Shymbulak backcountry
Pitch: A gondola from a big, cheap city straight into the Tian Shan: lift-served freeride above Shymbulak and a 4,000 m wall rising behind Almaty.

Name: Trans-Ili Alatau huts & yurts
Pitch: Multi-day touring from yurts, mountain huts and an old Soviet observatory: Bogdanovich Glacier above Shymbulak, the Turgen Gorge, and the Ketmen ridge to the east.

Name: Karakol & Tian Shan
Pitch: Adventure: a small resort plus yurt-based touring and cat skiing in dry continental powder.

Name: Kosciuszko Main Range
Pitch: Australia's alpine high point: day and overnight touring from Thredbo/Charlotte Pass; Western Faces.

Name: Snowy Mountains (Thredbo, Perisher)
Pitch: Australia's biggest areas; snowmaking-dependent, variable natural snow.

Name: Victorian Alps (Falls Creek, Hotham, Buller)
Includes: Falls Creek; Mt Hotham; Mt Buller
Pitch: Melbourne's playground; Hotham has the most expert terrain in Australia.

Name: Mt Hutt
Pitch: Big open bowl above the Canterbury Plains; Methven heli nearby.

Name: Mt Ruapehu
Pitch: Active volcano in the North Island with crater-lake ski touring; variable conditions.

Name: NZ Club Fields (Craigieburn, Broken River, Temple Basin)
Pitch: Rope tows with nutcrackers, steep ungroomed terrain, club lodges. Unique and cheap.

Name: Queenstown & Wanaka
Includes: The Remarkables; Coronet Peak; Cardrona; Treble Cone
Pitch: Four resorts (Remarkables, Coronet Peak, Cardrona, Treble Cone) and the adventure capital; heli everywhere.

Name: Southern Alps Heli & Tasman Glacier
Pitch: Big-day heli from Wanaka/Methven/Queenstown, and ski-plane runs on the Tasman Glacier under Aoraki.

Name: Mauna Kea
Pitch: Ski a 4,200 m tropical volcano by 4x4 shuttle, then surf the same day. Only after rare winter storms, so it's an opportunistic trip.
